recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-14694 unless Vocabulary creates a new final Jira decision changing include.valueSet semantics again.
issue_request: FHIR-14694 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked to clarify ValueSet.compose.include.valueSet cardinality and whether multiple referenced value sets were intersected or joined; the final resolution retained singular element wording but said multiple valueSet references included the union of all referenced value-set contents.
initial_application: The issue was pre-applied in SVN r13351, represented in git as d90f55e1cb, which updated source/valueset/valueset-spreadsheet.xml with the seed's short text and union definition. Later source refactors moved the active ValueSet definition into source/valueset/structuredefinition-ValueSet.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-25179 was a later Published/Persuasive R5 Vocabulary decision for the same element and explicitly changed this sentence from union to intersection, with matching expansion-algorithm guidance. FHIR-30574 later raised the same apparent inconsistency and was closed Resolved - No Change / Not Persuasive as duplicate/background. The combined branch already contains bbb15e86e66f453d528c4dde1a08846ded2f63f0 auditing FHIR-25179, so that related issue was not republished.
reconciliation: An empty audit commit was published. The active ValueSet resource is in build scope through source/fhir.ini, the current structure definition says multiple valueSet references within one include use the intersection of referenced contents, and the Value Set Expansion narrative also describes intersecting the referenced value-set result sets. Restoring the seed's older union sentence would undo the later final FHIR-25179 decision.
